assumed_answer: Code Orange = spill of 500 mL or more of a hazardous chemical/biological agent, OR any amount of a highly toxic, reactive, flammable or explosive substance, OR any spill the person cannot safely contain; smaller low-hazard spills are handled locally with the spill kit and reported to the cleaning supervisor. Drop the '< 1 L minor spill' wording.
basis: No Saudi national volume threshold exists; hospital policies vary (risk-based or 50 mL–4 L). 500 mL is a common mid-point and matches the program D1 recommendation.

assumed_answer: Use this 11-code set until the poster arrives: Red fire; Orange hazardous spill; White violent/aggressive person (no weapon); Silver person with a weapon/hostage; Black bomb threat; Pink infant/child abduction or missing child; Blue cardiac/respiratory arrest (2222); RRT deteriorating patient; Yellow external disaster/mass casualty; Grey severe weather (sandstorm/flood); Brown utility failure. Announcements: 'Code [colour] + location' and 'Code [colour] all clear'. All extensions except 2222 = placeholder until client confirms.
basis: Saudi has no single MOH colour standard (Riyadh survey found 34 codes, only Red consistent); set is taken from the source deck. 2222 is the Saudi Health Council unified CPR number for all government and private hospitals.

assumed_answer: Occupational effective dose limit 20 mSv/year averaged over 5 years (100 mSv/5 y, no single year > 50 mSv); public 1 mSv/year; lens of eye 20 mSv/year; pregnant worker 1 mSv to the fetus for the rest of the pregnancy. Treat 1.25 and 3.75 mSv as per-quarter ALARA investigation levels (Level I review / Level II investigation), not dose limits; drop '2 mSv / 3 months' unless the RSO confirms it is a facility action level.
